text: Newborn, born after the 32nd gestational week. The baby was born via cesarean delivery. The mother had gestational diabetes but was otherwise healthy with no other pregnancy-related diseases.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you. Given the premature birth and maternal diabetes, I need to assess the severity of the respiratory distress. Is the baby exhibiting grunting, nasal flaring, or retractions, and are they currently requiring supplemental oxygen or mechanical ventilation?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Respiratory distress. I also have Tachypnea, Subcostal and intercostal retractions, Nasal flaring, Cyanosis.

speaker: Doctor
text: The clinical picture of a premature infant with maternal diabetes and significant respiratory distress strongly suggests Respiratory Distress Syndrome due to surfactant deficiency. REQUEST TEST: Chest_X-Ray

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Ground-glass appearance, air bronchograms, suggesting Respiratory Distress Syndrome (RDS)

speaker: Doctor
text: The chest X-ray findings of ground-glass appearance and air bronchograms, combined with the clinical history of prematurity and maternal diabetes, are classic for Respiratory Distress Syndrome. DIAGNOSIS READY: Respiratory Distress Syndrome (RDS)
